# Chota Namu supplied character files

Namdev Shirodkar supplied the PNG and GIF on 15 October 2026 and instructed the implementation agent to use them for Quiz Show Kit and publish the repository update. The original bytes are preserved. The uploader identified these as the actual Chota Namu assets; no replacement likeness or artwork was generated.

| File | Supplied filename | Use in this project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chota-namu.png` | `02-1000495459.png` | Optional static character artwork for entry and About/settings areas |
| `chota-namu-idle.gif` | `01-1000495472.gif` | Preserved animation/reference source; not embedded or automatically played by the quiz runtime |

The PNG is a transparent 572 × 1281 image. The GIF is a 384 × 256, 73-frame idle showcase with its own caption and background. File dimensions, sizes and SHA256 hashes are recorded in `PROVENANCE.json` and the asset catalog. Neither file was resized, cropped, cleaned up, recolored, recompressed or otherwise edited.

This notice records project-specific user authorization. It does not grant permission for unrelated reuse or general redistribution, does not relicense the character under the software's MIT license, and does not claim that the original artist or any underlying third-party rights were independently verified. Ask the relevant rights holder before using these character files outside this project. Public repository availability is not a general artwork license or an institutional endorsement.

Retain this notice and the provenance record with copies distributed as part of the authorized project. The character may be omitted by a teacher or event configuration. No pointer tracking, remote data collection, or interactive gaze is provided by these original files.

questions.stem: In a typical human body cell, which structure contains most of the cell's DNA?
questions.explanation: The nucleus encloses the chromosomes, which contain most of a typical human cell's DNA. Mitochondria also contain a small amount of DNA, so saying that every DNA molecule is in the nucleus would be inaccurate.

questions.stem: Which gas is taken up from inhaled air to support cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Gas exchange brings oxygen from inhaled air into the bloodstream while carbon dioxide leaves the blood to be exhaled. The lungs and circulation therefore help supply oxygen to the body's cells.

questions.stem: A cell is actively assembling amino acids into new proteins. Which cellular structure directly carries out this assembly?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes assemble amino acids into proteins using information carried by messenger RNA. They may occur freely in the cytoplasm or attach to the rough endoplasmic reticulum, depending on the protein being produced.

questions.stem: Blood filtration and selective reabsorption help remove wastes while retaining needed substances. Which organs perform this process to produce urine?
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains nephrons. Their glomeruli filter blood, and their tubules return needed substances to the circulation while helping remove wastes. The remaining fluid becomes urine, contributing to water and chemical balance.

sources.title: NIDDK — Your Kidneys and How They Work

questions.stem: An animal cell is placed in a solution with a lower concentration of dissolved, nonpenetrating solute particles than its cytoplasm. Its membrane lets water cross. What initially happens?
options: Net water leaves; the cell shrinks
No net water movement; size is unchanged
Net water enters; the cell swells
Water stops crossing; the cell becomes rigid
questions.explanation: The outside solution is hypotonic relative to the cell. Water moves into the cell by osmosis, increasing its volume. Because an animal cell lacks a rigid cell wall, excessive swelling can eventually rupture it.

questions.stem: At a fixed temperature, a catalyst is added to a reversible reaction. Which statement correctly describes its effect?
options: It speeds equilibration and always increases the final product fraction
It slows equilibration without changing the equilibrium composition
It changes the equilibrium composition without affecting reaction rates
It speeds equilibration without changing the equilibrium composition
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides a reaction pathway with a lower activation barrier. It increases both forward and reverse reaction rates, so equilibrium is reached sooner; it does not change the equilibrium composition at a fixed temperature.

questions.stem: A compound microscope uses a 10× eyepiece and a 40× objective. What is its total magnification?
questions.explanation: For a compound light microscope, multiply the eyepiece magnification by the objective magnification. Here, 10 times 40 gives 400. Adding the two numbers does not give the instrument's total magnification.

questions.stem: A laboratory bottle contains 250 millilitres of liquid. What is the same volume in litres?
questions.explanation: The prefix milli means one thousandth. Therefore, one litre contains 1,000 millilitres, and 250 millilitres equals 250 divided by 1,000 litres: 0.25 litres.

questions.stem: Which statement about gloves and hand hygiene in healthcare is correct?
options: Clean gloves replace hand hygiene for the whole shift
Hand hygiene is needed only when gloves visibly tear
Hand hygiene after removing gloves is unnecessary
Gloves do not replace hand hygiene
questions.explanation: Gloves provide a protective barrier but do not replace hand hygiene. Hands can become contaminated during glove use or removal. CDC recommends cleaning hands at the indicated moments, including after removing gloves.

sources.title: CDC — Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers

questions.stem: Why do antibacterial antibiotics not directly treat an ordinary viral cold?
options: They act only when a virus has caused a fever
They target only viruses outside the respiratory tract
They act against bacteria, not the cold-causing virus
They become antiviral when the dose is increased
questions.explanation: Antibacterial antibiotics treat certain bacterial infections and do not act against the viruses that cause ordinary colds. Using them unnecessarily offers no benefit against that virus and can still cause adverse effects.

sources.title: CDC — Healthy Habits: Antibiotic Do's and Don'ts

questions.stem: Researchers link resistant bacteria in patients, livestock and nearby water. Which response best reflects One Health?
options: Investigate human health separately from animal and environmental health
Integrate human, animal and environmental health investigations
Investigate animal health separately from human and environmental health
Investigate environmental health separately from human and animal health
questions.explanation: One Health recognises the connections among people, animals, plants and their shared environment. Coordinated work across these areas can help address problems such as infections and antimicrobial resistance that cross traditional departmental boundaries.

questions.stem: A balance repeatedly reads 10.8 g for a reference mass whose accepted value is 10.0 g. Which description best fits these measurements?
questions.explanation: The readings closely agree with each other, indicating high precision or repeatability. Their consistent difference from the reference value indicates poor accuracy. Repeating a measurement does not by itself remove a systematic error.

questions.stem: In genetics, what does DNA stand for?
questions.explanation: DNA means deoxyribonucleic acid. It carries genetic information, and its sequence helps specify the development and functioning of organisms. The abbreviation describes a particular nucleic acid rather than a protein or an organelle.

questions.stem: In cellular metabolism, what does ATP stand for?
questions.explanation: ATP means adenosine triphosphate. It couples energy-releasing processes to cellular work, such as transport and biosynthesis. Its name reflects the adenosine group and the three attached phosphate groups.

questions.stem: In a laboratory method that amplifies a chosen segment of DNA, what does PCR stand for?
questions.explanation: PCR means polymerase chain reaction. Repeated cycles use primers and a DNA polymerase to produce many copies of a selected DNA segment, allowing researchers to study an initially small amount of material.

questions.stem: In medical imaging, what does MRI stand for?
questions.explanation: MRI means magnetic resonance imaging. It uses strong magnetic fields and radiofrequency signals to obtain detailed internal images. It differs from X-ray imaging because the image formation does not use ionising X-rays.

questions.stem: A screening test identifies 80 of 100 people who truly have the condition. In this group, what is the test's sensitivity?
options: Cannot be calculated without counting healthy people
questions.explanation: Sensitivity describes detection among people who truly have the condition. In this example, 80 of the 100 actual cases test positive, giving 80% sensitivity; the remaining 20 cases are false negatives.

sources.title: Google for Developers — Accuracy, Recall, Precision and Related Metrics

questions.stem: At the start of a year, 40 townspeople already have a disease. During that year, 12 others become new cases. What is the incident-case count for that year?
questions.explanation: Incidence concerns new cases during a specified period, so the incident-case count is 12. The 40 people who already had the disease are existing cases and do not become new cases merely because another year begins.

questions.stem: Which programming language is represented by this official two-snakes logo?
questions.explanation: The blue and yellow two-snakes device is the official Python logo. Python is a programming language used in many fields, including scientific computing; recognising its identity here requires no programming knowledge.

sources.title: Python Software Foundation — The Python Logo

questions.stem: The instrument in this schematic holds a slide on a stage. Which task is it designed to perform?
options: Measure the mass of a specimen
Maintain a sample at a fixed temperature
questions.explanation: A compound light microscope uses lenses and illumination to produce a magnified view of a specimen on a slide. Its stage positions the slide; the objective and eyepiece lenses contribute to the observed magnification.

visual.alt: Unlabelled schematic of a compound light microscope with an eyepiece, objectives and slide stage
visual.attribution: Original schematic; scientific function checked against OpenStax Microbiology, Instruments of Microscopy.

questions.stem: Which task best matches the handheld laboratory instrument shown?
options: Measure the mass of a dry powder
Determine the temperature of a sample
Transfer a measured small volume of liquid
questions.explanation: A micropipette transfers measured small liquid volumes using an appropriate tip and volume setting. The illustration represents this liquid-handling instrument; weighing, centrifugation and temperature measurement require different equipment.

visual.alt: Unlabelled schematic of a handheld micropipette with plunger and disposable tip
visual.attribution: Original schematic; function checked against Eppendorf official liquid-handling documentation.

questions.stem: What kind of hazard is indicated by this standard warning symbol?
questions.explanation: The biohazard symbol warns of a biological hazard, such as potentially infectious material. It communicates the need for appropriate precautions; it does not identify a specific organism or indicate that the material is radioactive.

sources.title: OSHA — Biological Hazards and Infectious Diseases

visual.alt: Standard three-lobed biological hazard warning symbol without a text label
visual.attribution: Standard biohazard symbol; identity checked against OSHA biological-hazards documentation.

questions.stem: In this schematic of double-stranded DNA, what forms the two outer backbones, or 'rails'?
options: Alternating amino acids and peptide bonds
questions.explanation: Each DNA strand has an outer backbone of alternating deoxyribose sugar and phosphate groups. The nitrogenous bases extend inward and pair between the strands, forming the ladder-like connections shown in this simplified diagram.

visual.alt: Schematic DNA double helix with two outer rails and connecting rungs, without component names
visual.attribution: Original simplified schematic; backbone structure checked against NHGRI DNA glossary.

questions.stem: An AI chatbot confidently cites a journal article that does not exist. What is this type of error commonly called?
questions.explanation: A hallucination is plausible-looking but factually incorrect generated content. A convincing citation can therefore be invented. Scientific claims and references should be checked against the original publication or another reliable source before being relied upon.

sources.title: Google for Developers — Machine Learning Glossary

questions.stem: Which description best captures machine learning?
options: Storing every fact without making any predictions
Learning useful patterns from data to make predictions or generate content
Following only a fixed rule written for every possible example
Measuring a sample without analysing its data
questions.explanation: Machine learning trains a model using data so it can make useful predictions or generate content. The learned relationships can be applied to new examples, but their reliability still depends on the data and evaluation.

sources.title: Google for Developers — What Is Machine Learning?

questions.stem: A previously trained image model is given a new microscope image and returns a prediction, without updating its learned parameters. What stage is this?
questions.explanation: Inference uses an already trained model to produce a prediction or response for a new input. Training changes the model's learned parameters. Simply supplying an input for a prediction does not automatically retrain the model.

sources.title: Google for Developers — Machine Learning Glossary

questions.stem: An AI study recruits only young adults but intends to serve people of every age. What is the clearest concern?
options: The sample may not represent the intended population
The sample guarantees equal performance at every age
The model becomes unbiased simply because it uses numbers
The sample removes the need for external evaluation
questions.explanation: Selecting only one age group can leave other intended users poorly represented. This is a form of selection or coverage bias. Performance should be checked on data representing the population where the model will be used.

sources.title: Google for Developers — Fairness: Types of Bias

questions.stem: A team repeatedly changes its model after checking the same final test set. Which statement best describes the resulting evaluation?
options: Its score remains independent because weights were fitted only on training data
Its score becomes independent once the same test rows are shuffled
Its score becomes independent by averaging repeated scores on those rows
Its score may be optimistic because decisions were tuned to that test set
questions.explanation: Repeatedly using final test results to guide model changes can adapt development to the test set's peculiarities. A separate validation set supports development, while an untouched final test set gives a more independent assessment.

sources.title: Google for Developers — Dividing the Original Dataset

questions.stem: Of 100 samples, 95 are negative and 5 are positive. An AI model labels every sample negative. Which conclusion is correct?
options: It has 5% accuracy and detects every positive sample
It has 95% accuracy and detects 95% of positive samples
It has 95% accuracy but detects none of the positive samples
It has 100% accuracy because negative samples are more common
questions.explanation: The model correctly labels the 95 negative samples, giving 95% overall accuracy. It misses all five positive samples, so its positive-case detection is zero. High accuracy can therefore conceal failure on a rare class.

sources.title: Google for Developers — Accuracy, Recall, Precision and Related Metrics

questions.stem: An AI transcription labels a body-temperature reading '37 kilograms'. Which unit fits the temperature reading instead?
questions.explanation: Temperature and mass are different physical quantities. Degrees Celsius can express a body-temperature reading, whereas kilograms express mass. Checking units is a simple way to catch an implausible transcription before using the result.

questions.stem: For dilute aqueous samples, the approximate hydrogen-ion concentration at pH 3 is how many times that at pH 5?
questions.explanation: The pH scale is logarithmic: each decrease of one pH unit corresponds approximately to ten times the hydrogen-ion concentration in a dilute aqueous solution. A decrease from pH 5 to pH 3 therefore corresponds to 100 times.

sources.title: USGS Water Science School — pH and Water

visual.alt: Two unlabelled sample containers displaying pH 3 and pH 5
visual.attribution: Original two-sample schematic; pH interpretation checked against USGS Water Science School, pH and Water.

questions.stem: Which process is intended to eliminate all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores, from an object?
questions.explanation: Sterilisation aims to eliminate all microbial forms, including bacterial spores. Cleaning removes material, while disinfection has different levels of microbial inactivation and does not necessarily eliminate spores. The terms are therefore not interchangeable.

sources.title: CDC — A Rational Approach to Disinfection and Sterilization

questions.stem: An AI report says two measured variables are correlated. Which statement is justified by that information alone?
options: The first variable has been proved to cause the second
The second variable has been proved to cause the first
They are associated; a causal effect has not been established
They cannot share any other influencing variable
questions.explanation: Correlation describes an association between variables. It does not by itself establish that changing one causes the other; shared influences or other explanations may exist. Causal conclusions need an appropriate study design and supporting evidence.

questions.stem: Which is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature?
questions.explanation: The kelvin is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature. Degrees Celsius are also used for temperature, but are not the base unit. Joules measure energy and watts measure power.

questions.stem: Which is the SI base unit of amount of substance?
questions.explanation: The mole is the SI base unit of amount of substance. It relates a sample to a specified number of elementary entities. Kilograms express mass, litres express volume, and pascals express pressure.

questions.stem: Which polysaccharide forms the main structural framework of plant cell walls?
questions.explanation: Cellulose forms the main structural framework of plant cell walls. These walls lie outside the plasma membrane, providing shape and structural support. Their rigid material helps explain why plants and animals differ in cell structure.

questions.stem: Which subunits are joined together to form a strand of RNA?
questions.explanation: RNA is a nucleic acid built from nucleotides. Each RNA nucleotide includes a ribose sugar, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base. The ordered nucleotide sequence carries information used in cellular processes.

questions.stem: In a sunlit grassland food web, which organisms initially capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy?
questions.explanation: Photosynthetic producers such as green plants capture solar energy and convert it into chemical energy. Consumers obtain energy by feeding on organisms or organic material rather than by directly capturing sunlight in this food web.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e — Energy Flow through Ecosystems

questions.stem: Which activity most directly returns nutrients from dead organic matter to the environment?
questions.explanation: Microbial decomposition breaks down dead organic material and contributes to nutrient cycling. This makes elements available for reuse in ecosystems. Predation, photosynthesis and pollination perform other roles and are not the same process.

questions.stem: Which of these is a unit of length?
questions.explanation: The metre is the SI base unit of length. Seconds measure time, kilograms measure mass, and kelvins measure thermodynamic temperature. This demonstration is unscored and does not use a participant's official answer attempt.

sources.title: NIST — SI Units
sources.supportNote: The NIST Base and Derived Units table was inspected for all four options: meter is the SI base unit of length, second of time, kilogram of mass, and kelvin of thermodynamic temperature.

optionExplanations: The second measures time, so it is not a length unit.
The metre measures length and is the correct choice.
